title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol: foresight of elects' faith inferred from election — Acts 13:48; Prosper on dignity
pass_a_gloss: But this being granted, election is not elicited from antecedent foresight of faith: but a certain foresight in God of the faith of the elect is inferred from antecedent election, according to that celebrated saying, Acts 13:48. As many as were ordained to eternal life believed. Whence also it may rightly be said that God foresees all those as about to believe, before they receive eternal life, whom by the decree of predestination he has ordained to receive this eternal life. What therefore Prosper said of charity, that we also constantly affirm of faith: Of this so great and so ineffable good no one has been found worthy: But whoever has been elected by God has been made worthy, On Free Will, p. 125. The most learned Father, and scourge of the Pelagians and Semipelagians, did not say, Whoever considered and foreseen by God himself as endowed with the gift of charity or faith, he afterward was elected by him, but, Whoever has been elected by God, he afterward has been made partaker of faith and charity.
pass_b_english: Granted that, election is not drawn from antecedent foresight of faith — rather a sure foresight in God of the elects' faith is inferred from antecedent election, per Acts 13:48: as many as were ordained to eternal life believed. So God rightly foresees as about to believe, before they receive eternal life, all whom by the predestination decree he ordained to receive it. What Prosper said of charity we also affirm of faith (On Free Will, p. 125): of this so great, ineffable good no one was found worthy; but whoever was elected by God was made worthy. That learned Father, scourge of Pelagians and Semipelagians, did not say: whoever considered and foreseen as endowed with charity or faith was afterward elected — but: whoever was elected by God afterward became partaker of faith and charity.
source_text: At hoc concesso non elicitur electio ex antecedanea fidei praevisione: sed certa in Deo fidei electorum praevisio infertur ex antecedanea electione, juxta illud celebre dictum, Actor. xiii. 48. Crediderunt quotquot ordinati fuerunt ad vitam aeternam. Unde etiam recte dicatur, Deum praevidere illos omnes crediturus, antequam accipiant vitam aeternam, quos decreto praedestinationis ad hanc vitam aeternam accipiendam ordinavit. Quod itaque Prosper de charitate dixit, id de fide etiam constanter affirmamus, Hoc tanto et tam ineffabili bono nemo inventus est dignus: Sed quicunque electus est a Deo, factus est dignus, de lib. arbit. pag. 125. Non dixit doctissimus Pater, et Pelagianorum ac Semipelagianorum Mastigium, Quicunque consideratus et praevisus ab ipso Deo ut dono charitatis aut fidei praeditus, ille postmodum ab eo electus est, sed, Quicunque a Deo electus est, ille postmodum fidei et charitatis factus est particeps.
